bib.title: SmolDocling: An ultra-compact vision-language model for end-to-end multi-modal document conversion
bib.venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "SmolDocling: An ultra-compact vision-language model for end-to-end multi-modal document conversion", Nassar, Marafioti, Omenetti, Lysak, Livathinos, Auer, Morin, Teixeira de Lima, Kim, Gurbuz, Dolfi, Farre, Staar (IBM Research, HuggingFace). arXiv:2503.11576v1, 14 Mar 2025 (the PDF prints no venue; ICCV 2025 comes from your OpenAlex note, not the PDF).
COVERAGE: All 24 pages extracted (77,717 chars). Body (pp1-9) and appendix A-C (pp15-24) read in full. References (pp10-14) skimmed only. Figure images on pp16-18 and 21-24 were not inspected, only their captions.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- claim: The recipe is three stages (a curriculum). Stage 1 adds DocTags as tokenizer tokens and freezes the vision encoder; everything else trains. Stage 2 unfreezes the vision encoder and trains on pretraining plus task-specific data. Stage 3 fine-tunes on all datasets.
  number: none
  setup: Sec 3.3. Section 5.1 does not repeat the freeze; it appears only in 3.3. No per-stage epoch counts or step counts are given.
  quote: "As an initial step, we incorporate DocTags as tokens in our tokenizer. To align the LLM part we freeze the vision encoder and train only the remaining network to adapt it to the new output format which it hasn't seen before. ... Next, we unfreeze the vision encoder and train the model on our pretraining datasets (see Sec. 4.1), along with all task-specific conversion datasets, including tables, code, equations, and charts. Finally, we fine-tune using all available datasets."
  where: p5 (Sec 3.3)
- claim: Hyperparameters and compute. The vision encoder, once unfrozen, gets a learning rate 100x lower than the rest. The paper gives no batch size, LoRA or adapter use, or per-stage epoch split.
  number: 2e-4 (rest), 2e-6 (vision encoder once unfrozen), 4 epochs, 64 A100 80GB, 38 h/epoch
  setup: Full fine-tune of SmolVLM-256M. AdamW, grad clip 1.0, warmup ratio 0.03. By my arithmetic that is about 152 h wall-clock, or about 9,700 A100-hours; the paper does not state this.
  quote: "Our training was conducted using 64 NVIDIA A100 80GB GPUs, with each epoch requiring 38 hours. The model was trained for a total of 4 epochs using the AdamW optimizer with a learning rate of 2 × 10−4 and 2 × 10−6 for the vision encoder once unfrozen. We also employed gradient clipping to 1.0 for stability and a warmup ratio of 0.03."
  where: p7 (Sec 5.1)
- claim: Inference is cheap. It also limits context and page count.
  number: 0.35 s/page, 0.489 GB VRAM, 8,192 tokens, up to 3 pages
  setup: vLLM on one A100.
  quote: "SmolDocling achieves a page conversion time of 0.35 seconds while occupying only 0.489 GB of VRAM. The model supports a maximum sequence length of 8,192 tokens and is trained to process up to three pages at a time."
  where: p7
- claim: Full-page text recognition beats larger models on every metric.
  number: Edit distance 0.48 vs 0.56 (Qwen2.5-VL 7B), 0.61 (GOT 580M), 0.62 (Nougat 350M); F1 0.80 vs 0.72/0.69/0.66
  setup: DocLayNet test, tables omitted, Markdown output, 144 DPI. Evaluation harness is the authors' own conversion of HTML or DocTags to Markdown.
  quote: "SmolDocling (Ours) 256M 0.48 0.80 0.89 0.79 0.58 0.67" and "SmolDocling significantly outperforms GOT, Nougat and also Qwen2.5-VL, which is 27 times larger, on every metric in full-page transcription"
  where: p7-8, Table 2
- claim: Equation recognition ties with GOT and is well ahead of Qwen2.5-VL and Nougat.
  number: SmolDocling edit 0.11 / F1 0.95, vs GOT 0.11 / 0.95, Qwen2.5-VL 0.22 / 0.89, Nougat 0.62 / 0.60
  setup: Im2Latex-230k, all outputs LaTeX-normalised with the same procedure used for SynthFormulaNet.
  quote: "SmolDocling (Ours) 256M 0.11 0.95 0.96 0.95 0.83 0.89"
  where: p7, Table 2
- claim: Code listings have no baseline because other models were not trained for the task.
  number: edit 0.11, F1 0.92
  setup: SynthCodeNet test, which is the authors' own synthetic data.
  quote: "SmolDocling (Ours) 256M 0.11 0.92 0.94 0.91 0.87 0.89"
  where: p7, Table 2
- claim: Layout mAP is better than Qwen2.5-VL-7B but far below human agreement, and the mAP is low in absolute terms.
  number: overall 0.231 vs 0.133 vs human 0.82
  setup: DocLayNet test, 6 mapped classes, mAP[0.5:0.95]. Picture is the exception (0.066 vs 0.078).
  quote: "Overall 0.231 0.133 0.82"
  where: p8, Table 3
- claim: Table structure is strong but cell text is weak on low-resolution crops.
  number: TEDS with text 0.52 (FinTabNet) and 0.65 (PubTables-1M); structure-only 0.81 and 0.88. TableFormer gets 0.89 and 0.84, but with external OCR.
  setup: Cropped tables at 72 dpi with compression artefacts. Also in Table 4: Granite Vision 2.98B 0.54 and SmolVLM 2.2B 0.18 on FinTabNet.
  quote: "SmolDocling (Ours) 256M 0.52 (0.81) 0.65 (0.88)"
  where: p9, Table 4
- claim: Chart-to-table is mid-pack.
  number: TEDS 0.75 vs Granite Vision 3B 0.95, Molmo-E 1B 0.54, Phi-3.5-vision 4B 0.40, SmolVLM 2.2B 0.02
  setup: Competitor numbers are taken from the Granite report [25], not re-run. The authors blame inconsistent ground-truth styles.
  quote: "SmolDocling (Ours) 256M 0.75"
  where: p9, Table 5
- claim: Architecture. The base is SmolVLM-256M (Idefics3-style). Parts: SigLIP base patch-16/512 (93M) vision encoder, SmolLM2 135M LLM, pixel shuffle giving 64 tokens per 512x512 patch.
  number: 93M, 135M, 64 tokens/patch, 4096 px/token
  setup: The base was already rebalanced toward documents. The paper also says it is "5 and 10 times smaller" than comparable document VLMs.
  quote: "SmolVLM-256M relies on SigLIP base patch-16/512 (93M) as visual backbone and compared to the 2.2B version of the same model, its training data was rebalanced to emphasize document understanding (41%) and image captioning (14%)"
  where: p4 (Sec 3.1)
- claim: Training data mix. Sizes are in Table 1; see the quotes.
  number: DocLayNet-PT 1.4M pages; Docmatix 1.3M docs / 9.5M DocVQA questions; DocLayNet v2 60K fine-tune pages (76K annotated); WordScape 63K; SynthDocNet 250K text (Table 1 says 375K); SynthChartNet 2.5M; SynthCodeNet 9.3M (56 languages in text, 57 in appendix); SynthFormulaNet 5.5M; Cauldron 2.63M; DocLayNet-PT-Instruct 1.62M; DocMatix w/ conversion 952K
  setup: Pretraining pages carry only weak labels, produced by Docling PDF parsing. Instruction data is built with rules plus Granite-3.1-2b-instruct. Cauldron is included "to avoid catastrophic forgetting". There are no stage-by-stage mixing ratios.
  quote: "DocLayNet-PT is a 1.4M pages dataset extracted from the DocFM dataset" and "Our dataset includes 9.3M million rendered code snippets generated at 120 dpi, covering 56 programming languages."
  where: p5-6, Table 1
- claim: DocTags is XML-like. Block tags (text, title, formula, otsl, code, picture, list_item and others) nest location tags. Table structure uses the OTSL vocabulary interleaved with text. Cropped elements use the same format as full pages.
  number: coordinates are integers 0-500; 14 layout classes
  setup: Appendix A.4 and Sec 3.2. Code carries a language tag. Pictures carry an image_class tag from a list of about 22 classes.
  quote: "Each element can nest additional standalone location tags that encode its position on the page as a bounding box, represented in DocTags as <loc_x1><loc_y1><loc_x2><loc_y2>. ... we used integer values in the range from 0 to 500"
  where: p19 (A.4); p4 (3.2)
- claim: The paper argues DocTags beats Markdown or HTML because it separates structure from content. It reports no ablation.
  number: none
  setup: Assertion only.
  quote: "This disentanglement improves performances of Image-to-Sequence models by minimizing confusions. In contrast, direct conversion to standard formats such as HTML or Markdown is often lossy and ambiguous"
  where: p4

LIMITS
- Failure modes the authors concede (p9): missing tags, malformed structure and endless token repetition; "fabricating non-existent text cells" is shown in the Table 7 caption (p22).
- Layout localisation is weak ("critical area requiring further refinement", p9).
- Cell-text transcription on low-resolution crops is weak: "insufficient training at such resolutions".
- Molecule recognition (App C.1) fails to reconstruct detailed structure; the paper reports no number.
- Not in the paper: no ablation of the staged freeze or unfreeze, the 2e-6 vs 2e-4 split, DocTags vs Markdown, or the data mix. No loss-masking or label-masking detail (the extraction has no mention of "mask" or "loss" for training). No LoRA. No batch size. No stage-wise epochs or learning rates. No safety or licence discussion. Datasets were "will be publicly available soon" in v1.
- Comparisons are on the authors' harness, with outputs mapped to common formats. Only Qwen2.5-VL 7B is compared on layout. Code has no baseline.
- Training is expensive: it is a near-full pretraining run, not a small fine-tune.

BUILDS ON: SmolVLM-256M [56] (Hugging Face), Idefics3 [41] and SigLIP, SmolLM2 (Allal et al. 2025), OTSL (Lysak et al. [55], the table markup), Docling (Auer et al. 2024) for weak labels, The Cauldron [42], Docmatix [41], MathWriting (Gervais et al. 2024), Nougat (Blecher et al. 2023), GOT [89], Qwen2.5-VL (Bai et al. 2025), DocOwl 2 [28].

CODE: none in the paper. The only snippets are the DocTags tag vocabulary on p19. Table 6 (p20) lists the prompts:
- "Convert this page to docling."
- "Convert chart to table (e.g., <chart>)."
- "Convert formula to LaTeX (e.g., <formula>)."
- "Convert code to text (e.g., <code>)."
- "Convert table to OTSL (e.g., <otsl>)."
- "OCR the text in a specific location: <loc_155><loc_233><loc_206><loc_237>"

FIGURES (the extraction tool lists 7)
- Fig 1, p2: architecture (vision encoder, projection and pooling, concatenated with prompt text embeddings, LLM, DocTags output). Best for the freeze/unfreeze discussion, because it labels the parts.
- Fig 2, p4: DocTags examples on real pages, with nested location, OTSL and code tags. Best for note 02.
- Fig 3, p15: treemap of dataset sizes.
- Figs 4-6, pp16-18: synthetic chart, code and formula samples.
- Fig 7, p21: molecule failure case.
- Table 7, pp22-24: layout visualisations. It is a table, not a figure.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. Table 2 is flattened in the extraction, so rows run together; I re-read the numbers against the text. Table 1 also extracts jumbled. Its sizes are as printed, but their grouping into categories is uncertain. Internal inconsistencies: SynthDocNet is 250K in the p5 text and 375K in Table 1; code languages are 56 on p6 and 57 on p19. The caller's guess "does section 5.1 say freeze vision encoder?" is no: the freeze is in Sec 3.3 (p5), and 5.1 gives only the 2e-6 rate "once unfrozen".
